industry.size: Indian tyre industry revenue ~₹1.36 lakh cr in FY26; the top six makers are ~85% of it (CRISIL, 24-Aug-2026)
industry.fy27: CRISIL (24-Aug-2026): volume growth slows to 4-5% in FY27 after 7-8% in FY26; key inputs up 35-40%; natural rubber ~₹275/kg in Jun-2026 vs ~₹220/kg in FY26; operating margin down 200-250 bp to ~11.5-12% in FY27 (from ~14.2%), recovering to 13-13.5% in FY28 if input costs stabilise; "a cost-pass-through lag rather than a structural profitability reset"; the top six plan ~₹18,000 cr of capex over FY27-28, nearly double the previous two years
industry.rubber: Kottayam RSS-4 ₹273/kg on 3-Sep-2026; global futures near the highest since 2013 (Procurement Resource, 10-Sep-2026). CEAT (17-Jul-2026): domestic ~₹280/kg, a ₹15-20 premium to import parity; SICOM $2,180-2,200/t; two-thirds of its natural rubber is imported
industry.priceHikes: Industry took 7-9% of price increases by Q1FY27 with more planned in Q2 (CLSA via Moneycontrol, 12-Aug-2026); CEAT ~11% in replacement by mid-July and 4-6% more planned; MRF and others raised prices "in different measures, in different categories" (CEAT MD, 17-Jul-2026)
industry.demand: GST on most tyres cut from 28% to 18% in Sep-2025 (farm tyres 18% to 5%) and lower GST on vehicles lifted replacement and OEM demand in H2FY26; CEAT expects mid-single-digit replacement growth in truck and car tyres and high single digits in two-wheelers, with El Nino and the West Asia conflict as risks (Q1FY27 call)
industry.oht: Off-highway construction tyres and tracks (Camso): a global niche led by Michelin/Camso, Bridgestone and others; US tariff 10% on Sri Lankan OHT tyres and tracks, 25% on the steel in tracks (Q1FY27 call)
industry.regulation: DGFT licensing of tyre imports since Jun-2020 limits Chinese imports; EPR for waste tyres; four Labour Codes effective 21-Nov-2025 (CEAT booked ₹58 cr of past-service cost)

critiques: Q1 PAT of ₹4 cr was hit by interest: a ₹48 cr Sri Lankan-rupee loss on a USD80 mn intra-group loan; FY27E EPS cut 22%.
Margins have likely bottomed; tight demand-supply should allow price increases to stick; Camso recovery is back-ended.
Margins have bottomed out and could improve gradually.
Raw-material inflation (16-18% q/q in Q1, 8-10% more in Q2) needs 15-16% of price increases; the risk is that competitors hold back.
